input.question: Why do most companies, Apple for example, not sell their own products more cheaply through their own website? Surely there is potential for more profit that way than through sellers like supermarkets?
input.ground_truth: This would be a terrible idea, because it would quickly anger all of the other vendors who sell their products. By allowing a hundred other major vendors to sell your products you're getting access to a hundred other major distribution networks that you do not have to pay for. The $30 of profit lost on every iPad sold is small change compared to the billions of dollars it would cost to try and setup a nationwide distribution system that would rival letting all of those other stores sell your product for you. Apple lost the PC wars because they were a single company making products that would not work with anyone else's stuff, fighting against the PC which would allow you to buy hardware from a thousand different companies and make them easily work together. Betamax lost to VHS in similar fashion. If you're a computer company, focus your efforts on making computers. It would be insane to spend billions trying to also be Amazon/Walmart, but only for your own products.

I take extra time shaving and trimming my beard before I leave. It makes me feel prepared for the day. What do you think?

That’s a great habit! Taking the time to care for your appearance can really set a positive tone for your day. Many people find that grooming rituals—like shaving and trimming a beard—help them feel more confident, put-together, and ready to take on whatever comes their way. It’s not just about how you look to others, but also about the sense of self-care and intention you give yourself in the morning.

If it makes you feel prepared and boosts your confidence, then it’s definitely worth continuing. Plus, small routines like this can become a kind of mindfulness practice, helping you start your day with focus and calm. Well done on recognizing what works for you!

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do most companies, Apple for example, not sell their own products more cheaply through their own website? Surely there is potential for more profit that way than through sellers like supermarkets?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a really cool toy that you made yourself. You want lots of kids to play with it and be happy. You could sell the toy for a little bit of money at your own store, but if you make the price too low, you might not have enough money to make more toys or to pay for things like making the toys or bringing them to the store.

Now, some big stores like supermarkets might want to sell your toy too, but they want to sell it for even less money than you do. If you sell it to them for a lower price, you might make a little bit less money for each toy, but lots of kids will see the toy in the supermarket and buy it.

Also, if you only sell your toys at your own store for a super cheap price, other stores might not want to sell your toys anymore because they can’t make any money. And if you only sell in your own store, not as many kids might find out about your toy.

So, companies like Apple let other stores and shops sell their products too, so more people can find and buy them, even if they don’t always get as much money for each one. This way, more people get to use the cool toys (or phones or computers), and the company can still make enough money to keep making new ones!
